schemas/ack.json.description: Response to any message. Uses errors[] array — a single message can fail multiple field validations. Created by Spear Systems (a Spear company). Open standard — Apache 2.0, free to implement.

errors.description: Zero or more error objects. Present when status = ERROR or REJECTED.

negotiation.description: LEP-0009 §5: the negotiation outcome carried on every ack for a quote/counter (and on the bid ack of a successful redemption), so a buyer never infers state from prose. Absent on a v1.1 exchange.

binding_expires_at.description: At or before the negotiation expires_at; the token is unusable at or after this instant.

binding_token.description: Present only when outcome = accepted. Single-use; returned exactly once (the ack to the accepting message). The platform stores only a hash.

price_cents.description: The accepted, countered, or refused price; absent on a refusal that carried no price.

original_message_id.description: ID of the message being acknowledged.

rejection_reason.$comment: Open enum — enables publisher automation (route invalid_phone to retry, duplicate to dedup, etc.)
rejection_reason.description: Structured rejection reason when status = REJECTED. Known values: invalid_phone, invalid_email, duplicate, out_of_geography, out_of_scope, credit_too_low, already_customer, data_quality_fail, compliance_fail, price_too_high, capacity_exceeded, consent_expired, litigator_flagged. Open enumeration.

schemas/ack.json.title: LCP Ack Message

schemas/batch.json.description: v1.2 (LEP-0001 W2-01): bounded batch submission. The batch is a loop over the single-item intake path — each item's payload is a lead payload validated by schemas/lead.json, authenticated, deduped, and persisted exactly as a single lead would be. The batch schema therefore fixes the per-item metadata (item_id, idempotency_key) and the item payload's container, never the lead's own field rules: an item whose lead payload is invalid is a per-item `rejected` receipt, not a whole-request schema failure. Created by Spear Systems (a Spear company). Open standard — Apache 2.0, free to implement.

items.description: LEP-0001 W2-01 caps a batch at 100 items; exceeding the cap is a whole-request 413 LCP-001, never a per-item rejection.

idempotency_key.description: Per-item idempotency key (LEP-0001: per-item idempotency). A replay returns the item's original result as a `duplicate` receipt (existing DUPLICATE/LCP-005 semantics at item granularity).

item_id.description: Stable per-item identifier, echoed in that item's receipt. It also seeds the synthesized lead envelope's deterministic message id, so a replay of the same item reuses the same message.

payload.description: A full-PII lead payload — the root object of schemas/lead.json, never an envelope and never a ping payload. It is validated per item against schemas/lead.json and the lifecycle intake rules; an invalid payload rejects that item only.

request_id.description: Caller-supplied request identifier, echoed in the per-item response so a client can correlate the receipt list with its own submission record.

schemas/batch.json.title: LCP Batch Message

schemas/bid.json.description: Buyer's response to a ping. Contains the bid price, accept/reject decision, and estimated contact speed. The platform collects bids from all pinged buyers and selects the winner. Created by Spear Systems (a Spear company). Open standard — Apache 2.0, free to implement.

bid_price_cents.description: Buyer's bid price in cents. Required when decision = accept. Ignored when decision = reject or pass.

buyer_reference.description: Buyer's internal reference for this bid (for tracking).

capacity_remaining.description: Buyer's remaining capacity after this bid. Helps the platform route future pings. Optional.

decision.description: accept = buyer wants the lead at bid_price_cents; reject = buyer does not want this lead; pass = buyer declines to bid (no reason).

estimated_contact_seconds.description: Buyer's estimated time-to-contact in seconds. Used by the platform for speed-to-contact routing. Optional.

fx_expires_at.description: v1.2 (LEP-0010 §3): canonical whole-second UTC end of the rate's validity; MUST be strictly later than fx_timestamp. REQUIRED with fx_rate.

fx_rate.description: v1.2 (LEP-0010 §3): native major units per 1 settlement (offer-currency) major unit. Same direction and pattern as post.pricing.fx_rate. REQUIRED when bid.currency differs from the offer's currency; MUST NOT be relied on otherwise — on a same-currency bid the FX fields are inert and ignored for comparison (still schema-validated).

fx_source.description: v1.2 (LEP-0010 §3): named rate provider, or the literal 'bilateral' for a rate the two parties agreed directly. Compared by exact byte equality. REQUIRED with fx_rate.

fx_timestamp.description: v1.2 (LEP-0010 §3): canonical whole-second UTC instant the rate was observed (LEP-0002 canonical form). REQUIRED with fx_rate.

negotiation_binding_token.description: v1.2 (LEP-0009 C7): single-use token returned on a negotiation accept. It replaces bid_price_cents on this bid (the token carries the agreed price); a sender presents it only toward a receiver advertising `negotiation` and a parsed lcp_versions element of 1.2.0 or later.

ping_id.description: ID of the ping being responded to.

reject_reason.description: Why the buyer rejected (e.g. out_of_hours, capacity_full, vertical_mismatch, price_too_low). Open enumeration. Optional.

slots_claimed.description: v1.1 (LEP-0003 §2): buyer slots this buyer claims if selected. The claim is a request, not a reservation — the platform awards slots at post time (delivery is the claim event; bids are non-binding). Only meaningful with decision 'accept'; absent = 1. Capped at exactly 1 for v1.1: multi-slot agency claims (N > 1) have no delivery path on the per-(lead, offer) award guard and no awarded-count wire signal, so they are deferred (LEP-0003 Deferred questions, #153 T5) — this schema enforces maximum: 1 now. Capability-gated (SPEC.md §8): senders MUST NOT include v1.1 slot fields toward receivers whose lcp_versions advertisement does not parse to major == 1, minor >= 1.

schemas/bid.json.title: LCP Bid Message

schemas/call.json.description: Telephony lead message. Structurally distinct from form-based lead — carries call-specific blocks (IVR, durations, recording, disposition). Created by Spear Systems (a Spear company). Open standard — Apache 2.0, free to implement.

did.description: Dialed number (Direct Inward Dial) — the tracking number the consumer called.

forwarded_to.description: Number the call was forwarded to (buyer's destination number). E.164.

ivr.description: IVR menu interaction data. Core fields are universal; platform-specific IVR data goes in extensions.

abandoned.description: True if the caller dropped during IVR before reaching an agent.

menu_options_selected.description: Ordered list of menu option labels selected.

path.description: IVR menu path taken (e.g. 'sales > mortgage > refinance').

queue.description: Call queue that handled this call.

status.description: OPEN ENUMERATION — known values: answered, no_answer, busy, failed, voicemail. Unknown values MUST be stored and passed through.

tracking_number.description: Tracking/marketing number assigned to this campaign (may differ from DID if call was routed through a tracking pool). E.164.

transferred_from.description: Present if this call was transferred from another call/queue.

submitted_at.description: When the call was initiated (distinct from provenance.received_at).

schemas/call.json.title: LCP Call Message

attachments.description: Metadata for encrypted, out-of-band files. Binary content is never embedded in an LCP JSON envelope.

malware_scan.description: Non-sensitive malware scan evidence. A production attachment must have status clean before release.

residency.description: Country or deployment region where the attachment bytes are stored and scanned.

attributes.description: Vertical-specific fields. Shape defined by per-vertical JSON Schema in verticals/.
attributes.title: Attributes

consent_purposes.description: What was consented to (e.g. calls, sms, email, share_with_partners).

otp.description: OTP verification details. The actual OTP code MUST NOT be included.

consent_evidence_entry.description: A single piece of consent or compliance evidence.

provider.description: Vendor or system (e.g. jornaya, trustedform, internal).

token_or_url.description: Verification token, certificate URL, or reference.

type.description: Consent framework or evidence type (e.g. tcpa_consent, gdpr_opt_in).

consent_evidence_entry.title: Consent Evidence Entry

consumer.description: The person the lead is about.

email_hash.description: HMAC-SHA256(shared_secret, normalized_email). For dedup in ping. Same per-pair model as phone_hash.

full_name.description: Unstructured name — use when Western given/family splitting does not apply.

preferred_contact_method.description: Consumer's preferred contact method. Affects contact strategy and compliance.

secondary_phone.description: Secondary phone (work, spouse, alternate). E.164. Optional.

consumer.title: Consumer

street_address.description: Residential street address. Not ping-safe; omitted from ping payloads.

ip_address.description: Consumer IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) captured server-side. Post-only; not ping-safe. ip_hash remains the ping-safe projection.

schemas/core.json.description: Shared definitions for the LCP canonical core. Referenced by message-type and vertical schemas via $ref. Created by Spear Systems (a Spear company). Open standard — Apache 2.0, free to implement.
schemas/core.json.title: LCP Core Definitions

schemas/counter.json.description: Either party answers the standing negotiation message (LEP-0009). Strict allowlist: integer minor units, ISO 4217 currency, opaque ids, round counters, and closed/known reason values only. No consumer PII and no free text. Created by Spear Systems (a Spear company). Open standard — Apache 2.0, free to implement.

decision.description: counter = move the price; accept = close at the price of the message being answered; refuse = close with a reason.

expires_at.description: The negotiation's absolute end, unchanged. MUST NOT exceed the value set by the opening quote.

floor_price_cents.description: Restated and checked against the negotiation's floor (LCP-100 on mismatch).

negotiation_id.description: MUST name an existing negotiation for this (tenant, buyer, ping) triple; otherwise unknown_negotiation (or LCP-002 when it belongs to another buyer/tenant).

offer_id.description: MUST equal the negotiation's offer (LCP-100 on mismatch).

ping_id.description: MUST equal the negotiation's ping (LCP-100 on mismatch).

price_cents.description: Required unless decision = refuse. counter: subject to the monotone rule and at or above floor_price_cents. accept: MUST equal the price of the message it answers.

rejection_reason.description: Open enumeration. Required when decision = refuse; absent otherwise. Known values: below_floor_price, non_monotone_counter, round_limit_exceeded, negotiation_expired, unknown_negotiation, negotiation_closed.

rounds_remaining.description: The sender's view of the buyer counters still available at the moment this message is sent, before it is applied. A stale value is LCP-100.

schemas/counter.json.title: LCP Counter Message

schemas/envelope.json.description: Top-level LCP wrapper. Transport-agnostic. Payload shape is determined by message.type. Created by Spear Systems (a Spear company). Open standard — Apache 2.0, free to implement.

then.description: LEP-0009 C1/C2: negotiation types exist from protocol 1.2.0 (MINOR); a later major is a different contract and never rides this pattern.

correlation_id.description: Correlates this message with a prior message (e.g. ping → bid response).

idempotency_key.description: Idempotency key — duplicate submissions with the same key return the original result.

security.description: Transport-neutral HMAC signature. Optional for HTTP (headers used instead); required for non-HTTP transports.

test.description: Test message. Mirrored as X-LCP-Test header in the HTTP binding.

type.description: Message type. Closed enumeration — unknown types trigger LCP-006. `quote`/`counter` are the LEP-0009 negotiation types, emitted only toward a peer advertising `negotiation` and a parsed lcp_versions element of 1.2.0 or later. `subscription` is the LEP-0001 W3 registration type, emitted only toward a receiver advertising `event_subscriptions`.

payload.description: Message payload. Shape determined by message.type — see message-type schemas (lead.json, call.json, ping.json, post.json, ack.json, event.json, bid.json, batch.json, quote.json, counter.json, subscription.json).

schemas/envelope.json.title: LCP Envelope

schemas/event.json.description: Lifecycle notification. Events are open enumeration — receivers must store/pass through unknown values. Created by Spear Systems (a Spear company). Open standard — Apache 2.0, free to implement.

event.$comment: No enum constraint — this is an open enumeration per SPEC.md §6. Receivers must accept any string value.
event.description: Lifecycle event. OPEN ENUMERATION — known values: DELIVERED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, DISPUTED, REFUNDED, EXPIRED, CONVERTED, ARCHIVED. Unknown values MUST be stored and passed through, not rejected. Adding new values is a MINOR version bump, not breaking.

schemas/event.json.title: LCP Event Message

schemas/lead.json.description: Intake message — form/chat/click/api/agent/referral channel. Created by Spear Systems (a Spear company). Open standard — Apache 2.0, free to implement.

contact_window.description: Optional. Publisher hint for when the consumer is available to be contacted.

days.description: Days of week the consumer is available.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for the window times (e.g. Australia/Sydney).

extensions.description: v1.1 (LEP-0006 Track B): namespaced deployment-specific data (SPEC.md section 6; governance/EXTENSION-REGISTRY.md). Keys MUST follow {org}.{division}.{purpose} - at least three lowercase dot-separated segments - and lcp.core.* is reserved for the core. Values stay deployment-defined: the core does not and cannot validate namespaced payloads. Shape authority for a registered namespace is its record (LEP-0006 section B.2 defines {org}.form.questions: at most 25 entries of question_id/question_text/answer_text, question_text at most 300 and answer_text at most 1000 characters). These are receiver rules, not schema rules: a receiver that implements a registered form.questions namespace MUST validate entries and accept or reject the message (LCP-100), while receivers that do not recognize a namespace ignore its value. Bound hierarchy (LEP-0006 section B.2): the registered form.questions shape ceiling is 133,140 B worst-case UTF-8, receivers SHOULD reject extension totals above the 32 KiB soft policy target (a fully shape-conformant sender can exceed it; issue #197 tracks the re-tune), and the operative hard bound is the transport body cap (max_body_bytes, default 2,000,000 B). Never ping_safe: this field exists only on lead and post - ping/bid/ack keep their strict allowlists - and a platform MUST NOT derive ping attributes, compliance_flags, or any other ping field from extension content. Extension content is lead/post PII-scope content: it inherits section 9 retention and erasure, and question/answer text MUST NOT carry contact values, government identifiers, payment credentials, consent tokens, or evidence values (those have structured homes in consumer, compliance.consent_evidence[], and attachments[]).

lead_quality.description: Optional. Publisher-provided quality signals. Buyers use these to filter/route. All fields are publisher-declared and not independently verified by LCP.

data_completeness.description: How complete the lead data is. 'minimal' = name+phone only, 'standard' = core fields, 'rich' = core + vertical attributes fully populated.

duplicate_risk.description: Publisher's assessment of duplicate risk based on their dedup window.

spam_risk_score.description: Publisher's spam risk score (0 = clean, 100 = likely spam). Scoring methodology is publisher-defined.

verification.description: Details on how phone/email were verified. Supports OTP, enrichment tools, carrier lookup, SMTP validation, etc.

email_method.$comment: Open enum — new email verification services are additive.
email_method.description: How the email was verified. Known values: otp, smtp_check, bounce_check, briteverify, zerobounce, kickbox, none. Open enumeration.

email_verified_by.description: Provider that performed the verification (e.g. briteverify, zerobounce, internal, publisher_otp).

phone_method.$comment: Open enum — new verification methods (e.g. new enrichment providers) are additive.
phone_method.description: How the phone was verified. Known values: otp, carrier_lookup, call_connect, twilio_lookup, manual_call, none. Open enumeration.

phone_verified_by.description: Provider that performed the verification (e.g. twilio, numverify, internal, publisher_otp).

verified_email.description: Email was verified (OTP, bounce check, or SMTP validation).

verified_phone.description: Phone number was verified (OTP, call connect, or carrier lookup).

submitted_at.description: When the consumer submitted the lead (distinct from provenance.received_at which is when the platform received it).

schemas/lead.json.title: LCP Lead Message

schemas/offer.json.description: A buyer's published acceptance profile for lead routing. Offer administration is deployment-specific; this document is the interoperable discovery shape.

allowed_brand_ids.description: Optional publisher brand allowlist evaluated against provenance.brand_id.

allowed_publisher_ids.description: Optional publisher sender-ID allowlist. Matching fails closed when the incoming publisher is not listed.

attribute_equals.description: Safe declarative equality predicates keyed by vertical attribute name. Values are data, never executable expressions.

attribute_in.description: Safe declarative allowlists keyed by vertical attribute name.

call_routing_mode.description: post_call delivers recorded call metadata; realtime_transfer requires a separate telephony binding for the live bridge.

connect_timeout_seconds.description: Maximum time allowed for a real-time call transfer decision.

extensions.description: Namespaced deployment-specific criteria. Matching implementations must not execute arbitrary values as code.

monthly_maximum_payable.description: Optional hard maximum for payable outcomes in a calendar month.

monthly_minimum_payable.description: Operational pacing target for payable outcomes in each calendar month. It is not a guarantee of available supply.

monthly_quota_policy.description: monitor reports progress, pace prioritizes under-target offers, hard_cap stops payable routing at the maximum.

monthly_quota_timezone.description: IANA timezone used to determine the monthly quota period.

routing_mode.description: Direct sends a post at the floor price; auction sends a ping and waits for bids.

tenant_id.description: Owning platform tenant. Deployment metadata; not necessarily exposed in public offer discovery.

schemas/offer.json.title: LCP Buyer Offer

allOf.$comment: LEP-0003 §1/F8 (invalid example B): exclusive is exactly the one-slot special case. When the exclusivity hint is present and 'exclusive', slots_available MUST be 1 — an exclusive ping advertising more is a semantic error, rejected by this conditional, not just by prose. Absent slots_available stays legal (v1.0 behavior).

schemas/ping.json.description: Non-PII offer to buyers. STRICT ALLOWLIST — additionalProperties: false. No PII fields are permitted. The conformance runner also validates that every field in attributes is tagged ping_safe: true in the vertical schema. Created by Spear Systems (a Spear company). Open standard — Apache 2.0, free to implement.

attributes.description: Only fields tagged ping_safe: true in the vertical schema. Banded/aggregated only — never exact values.

compliance_flags.description: Presence indicators only — never tokens or evidence.

consent_valid.description: True if consent is still within its validity window (not expired).

dedup_window_hours.description: Sender hint: how many hours to dedup against. Optional.

email_hash.description: HMAC-SHA256(shared_secret, normalized_email) — per-pair, optional. Optional, for email-based dedup.

exclusivity.description: Hint to buyer: is this an exclusive or shared lead?

extensions.description: v1.2: optional namespaced extension container. The receiver admits a namespace on a ping ONLY when its registration declares ping safety (governance/EXTENSION-REGISTRY.md); every other namespace is refused by name. Values are bounded objects and never carry consumer PII.

lead_age_minutes.description: How many minutes since the consumer submitted the lead. Freshness signal for buyer pricing. Non-PII.

lead_reference.description: Opaque reference to the lead (not the lead_id).

offer_id.description: ID of the buyer offer this ping is being sent against. Enables audit trail for billing and disputes.

publisher_id.description: ID of the publisher that generated the lead. Non-PII — buyers need this for quality tracking and routing.

quality_flags.description: Non-PII quality signals for buyer filtering. All publisher-declared.

acquisition_method.description: paid_ad, organic_search, marketplace, gmb, cold_outbound, scraped, unknown. Open enum.

incentive_type.description: What incentive was offered (e.g. free_consultation, gift_card). Open enum.

is_incentivized.description: True if consumer was offered an incentive (free consultation, gift card, etc.).

slots_available.description: v1.1 (LEP-0003): remaining buyer-award slots of this lead that can still be sold at ping time, INCLUDING the slot this ping's recipient may win. A slot counts a distinct awarded buyer, never delivered copies (SPEC.md §3 slot semantics). For exclusivity 'exclusive' this MUST be 1 — the one-slot special case (enforced by the top-level conditional in this schema). Absent = the platform does not advertise slot state (v1.0 behavior). A platform MUST NOT send slots_available: 0; zero remaining means stop pinging. Non-PII integer count carrying no consumer data: it joins the ping strict allowlist as a reviewed non-PII field, and conformance keeps rejecting every other field outside the allowlist (LCP-008 PII_IN_PING protection preserved) and every attribute not tagged ping_safe: true in the vertical schema. Capability-gated (SPEC.md §8): senders MUST NOT include v1.1 slot fields toward receivers whose lcp_versions advertisement does not parse to major == 1, minor >= 1.

schemas/ping.json.title: LCP Ping Message

schemas/post.json.description: Full lead delivery to the winning buyer. Contains full PII. Created by Spear Systems (a Spear company). Open standard — Apache 2.0, free to implement.

call.description: Call detail block copied from a call intake when the post represents a call.

contacted_hashes.$comment: No uniqueItems (LEP-0003 §4): the wire array tolerates duplicates; the receiver merges by digest set per lead (at-least-once + set-union accumulation). maxItems 100: the record leaves the post-direction array bound open as a Deferred question ('a lead's contact attempts are naturally bounded'); this implementation bound is set generously above any realistic per-lead contact history so no conformant sender is clipped, while keeping the post payload bounded and rejecting bulk-suppression-sync misuse of this field (bulk sync stays out of scope; if production posts ever approach this bound, bulk routes to a dedicated mechanism). The CONTACTED event-report direction has its own tighter ingest bound (32 entries per report, SPEC.md §4).
contacted_hashes.description: v1.1 (LEP-0003 §3): parties already contacted for this lead by the publisher or prior slot holders, re-keyed under THIS receiving buyer's per-pair secret. Each entry is HMAC-SHA256(pair_secret, contact-preimage) — lowercase 64-hex, the same form as phone_hash (SPEC.md §9); the unsalted SHA-1-shaped digest of the reference network is explicitly NOT adopted (enumerable keyspaces invert it; §14 blocker B3). The platform matches digests only against values it holds in plaintext for this pair and cannot verify reported digests without the plaintext — the trust model is format + count sanity plus authenticated-sender attestation, scoped to one lead_id. Absent = the platform has no contact reports; [] = the platform attests no prior contacts (the two are distinct). Preimage rules and the phone-only/email-gated state are normative in SPEC.md §9. Capability-gated (SPEC.md §8): senders MUST NOT include v1.1 fields toward receivers whose lcp_versions advertisement does not parse to major == 1, minor >= 1.

extensions.description: v1.1 (LEP-0006 Track B): namespaced deployment-specific data (SPEC.md section 6; governance/EXTENSION-REGISTRY.md). Keys MUST follow {org}.{division}.{purpose} - at least three lowercase dot-separated segments - and lcp.core.* is reserved for the core. Values stay deployment-defined: the core does not and cannot validate namespaced payloads. Shape authority for a registered namespace is its record (LEP-0006 section B.2 defines {org}.form.questions: at most 25 entries of question_id/question_text/answer_text, question_text at most 300 and answer_text at most 1000 characters). These are receiver rules, not schema rules: a receiver that implements a registered form.questions namespace MUST validate entries and accept or reject the message (LCP-100), while receivers that do not recognize a namespace ignore its value. Bound hierarchy (LEP-0006 section B.2): the registered form.questions shape ceiling is 133,140 B worst-case UTF-8, receivers SHOULD reject extension totals above the 32 KiB soft policy target (a fully shape-conformant sender can exceed it; issue #197 tracks the re-tune), and the operative hard bound is the transport body cap (max_body_bytes, default 2,000,000 B). Never ping_safe: this field exists only on lead and post - ping/bid/ack keep their strict allowlists - and a platform MUST NOT derive ping attributes, compliance_flags, or any other ping field from extension content. Extension content is lead/post PII-scope content: it inherits section 9 retention and erasure, and question/answer text MUST NOT carry contact values, government identifiers, payment credentials, consent tokens, or evidence values (those have structured homes in consumer, compliance.consent_evidence[], and attachments[]).

matched_preferences.description: Buyer preferences that matched this lead.

offer_id.description: ID of the buyer offer that matched. Audit trail for billing and disputes.

dispute_window_expires_at.description: When the dispute window closes. Platforms mechanically reject disputes after this timestamp.

dispute_window_hours.description: Contractually agreed return window in hours. Buyer can dispute within this window.

fx_rate.description: LEP-0010 §4.1: native major units per 1 settlement major unit. Plain decimal — no sign, exponent, grouping or leading-zero integer part — with a mandatory fractional part of 6–12 digits, minimum six *significant* digits below 1, and a value in [0.000001, 1000000].

is_duplicate_resub.description: True if this is an accidental resubmission of a previously delivered lead.

payable_definition.$comment: Payable definition is agreed bilaterally between publisher and buyer. This field records which definition applies to this delivery.
payable_definition.description: What makes this lead payable (e.g. 'form_lead_valid_phone', 'call_answered_30s', 'connected_transfer', 'exclusive_delivery'). Open enumeration.

payable_status.description: Current payable status. 'pending' = within validation window, 'payable' = meets payable definition, 'not_payable' = failed validation, 'disputed' = under review.

submitted_at.description: When the consumer originally submitted the lead. Lets buyer assess lead age.

schemas/post.json.title: LCP Post Message

schemas/quote.json.description: Platform-opened, bounded price negotiation for a named ping (LEP-0009). Ping-class: integer minor units, ISO 4217 currency, opaque ids, timestamps, round counters, and closed/known reason values only. No consumer PII and no free text — the strict allowlist is the enforcement. Created by Spear Systems (a Spear company). Open standard — Apache 2.0, free to implement.

expires_at.description: Absolute end of the negotiation. MUST NOT be later than the ping's expires_at (or its timestamp plus TTL).

floor_price_cents.description: Restated from the ping so the buyer can verify the floor and the monotone rule without re-reading the ping.

max_rounds.description: Rounds this negotiation may run. Absent = 3 (D8 default); above the hard cap of 5 is LCP-100, never a deployment knob.

negotiation_id.description: Opaque platform-assigned negotiation id, unique per negotiation. The only lookup key a later message may use.

offer_id.description: The buyer offer being priced; MUST equal the ping's offer_id (LCP-100 on mismatch).

ping_id.description: The ping this negotiation prices. Supplies the floor, currency, and the TTL ceiling.

price_cents.description: The ask in minor units of currency. MUST be at or above floor_price_cents; below floor is refused below_floor_price and never clamped.

rejection_reason.description: Open enumeration. Present only on a terminal refusal message (no negotiation opened): below_floor_price, round_limit_exceeded, negotiation_expired, unknown_negotiation, negotiation_closed. When present, price_cents MUST be absent.

rounds_remaining.description: Buyer counters still available at the moment this message is sent. On the opening quote this equals the effective max_rounds (a quote consumes no round).

schemas/quote.json.title: LCP Quote Message

schemas/subscription.json.description: v1.2 (LEP-0001 W3): event-subscription registration and its resource view. The payload is a strict object: an explicit event allowlist drawn from the receiver's advertised `capabilities().events`, an HTTPS callback URL, and a filter whose keys are a closed set of core enums and identifiers. Consumer, provenance, attributes, details, contact, and security paths are never filter keys. The registration response carries `subscription_id`, `active`, `created_at`, and the per-subscription `secret` exactly once. Created by Spear Systems (a Spear company). Open standard — Apache 2.0, free to implement.

active.description: Subscription state. A disabled subscription receives no new deliveries.

callback_url.description: HTTPS callback destination (http only in an explicitly configured sandbox). Validated with the conformance runner's SSRF rule: no embedded credentials, a valid port, and only public resolved addresses.

created_at.description: Registration time in whole-second UTC form.

event_types.description: Explicit event allowlist. Values are the receiver's advertised event names; no wildcard and no second vocabulary exist. An unadvertised value is refused, never silently ignored.

filter.description: Closed filter over core enums and identifiers. Any other key, including consumer.email, provenance.*, and attributes.*, is refused with a named error.

replay_from.description: Opaque cursor from GET /v1/lcp/events. A subscription created with it replays that event set deterministically; an expired cursor is an explicit error.

secret.description: Per-subscription HMAC secret. Returned exactly once on registration and never again; deliveries are signed with it over the LEP-0002 canonical input.

subscription_id.description: Opaque subscription identifier returned on registration. It is not a bearer credential: every read, disable, and delivery is authorized against the subscriber's tenant.

schemas/subscription.json.title: LCP Subscription Message

verticals/home_services.json.description: Home services lead attributes. Every field is tagged ping_safe: true|false. Publishers normalize brand-specific form questions into this controlled taxonomy; unsupported source questions remain in an approved post-only extension or source archive.

exact_budget.description: Exact budget is post-only; use budget_band in a ping.
